title: A linear combination of elements defining an injective map is a nonzerodivisor in the polynomial ring
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if the map sending x to the tuple (x a_1, ..., x a_n) is injective, then the linear form sum a_i t_i is a nonzerodivisor in the polynomial ring, and the proof is a 29-line argument in two cases. The case of a Noetherian ring works with the associated primes of the base: for each associated prime one of the a_i is not a unit and the symmetric powers involved are free, so localising at that prime makes the multiplication injective and the injectivity follows because a map that is injective at all associated primes is injective. The general case writes the ring as a filtered union of Noetherian subrings containing the a_i and applies the result to each of them. The localisation argument at associated primes is the substance, and the reduction to the Noetherian case is displayed.
